documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: Provost-owned framework policy covering teaching, research and administration. It welcomes responsible use, sets data, disclosure, verification and procurement duties, and leaves classroom boundaries to instructors and syllabi.
documents.stance_why: The document says "The Augusta University (AU) community is encouraged to use these tools responsibly" but on academic use says "instructors and faculty should explicitly outline their AI use expectations" and "Students using AI must follow individual instructors’ expectations", so it sets no course-level rule and hands the decision to instructors.

units.why: Policy statement says "The Augusta University (AU) community is encouraged to use these tools responsibly", a default welcoming stance toward AI, addressed to everyone, so general phase, should, P02 and encourage; P56 not chosen because the sentence sets a default attitude, not a framework.
units.anchor: community is encouraged to use these tools responsibly
units.frag_start: The Augusta University (AU) community is encouraged

units.why: "The intent of this policy is to provide general guidance on the use of AI at AU" states the policy purpose, an institution-level framework preamble, so P56, informs, neutral.
units.anchor: provide general guidance on the use of AI at AU
units.frag_start: The intent of this policy is
units.policy: The policy's intent is to provide general guidance on the use of AI at AU.

units.why: "This policy applies to all faculty, staff, and students" sets who and what the policy covers (teaching, learning, research, administration), a scope statement within the framework, so P56 and general.
units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, and students at the university
units.policy: The policy applies to all faculty, staff, and students and governs the use of AI in teaching, learning, research, administrative functions, and scholarly communication.

units.why: "Users should be cognizant ... the use of AI in some countries may not be permitted in others" asks users to consider the global impact of choosing to use AI. It fits no type on legal reach across countries, so it is UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: think about the impacts of their decision to use AI
units.policy: Users should think about the impacts of their decision to use AI, because the use of AI in some countries may not be permitted in others.
units.uncovered_note: Users should consider cross-border legal differences when deciding to use AI.

units.why: The definition "Generative AI includes any machine-based tool designed to consider user questions, prompts" defines what the policy covers, so P61, informs, neutral.
units.anchor: Generative AI includes any machine-based tool designed to consider user questions

units.why: The phrase "offerings that are embedded in other software" extends the definition of generative AI to AI built into other products, which is the P07 concern (embedded AI), not just the definition type P61, because it decides that embedded tools are in scope.
units.anchor: offerings that are embedded in other software
units.policy: Generative AI includes both standalone offerings such as ChatGPT, Bard, Stable Diffusion, and offerings that are embedded in other software.

units.why: The definition "An AI agent is a system that uses artificial intelligence to autonomously perceive its environment" sets what an agent is for the policy, so P61 and informs.
units.anchor: AI agent is a system that uses artificial intelligence to autonomously perceive its environment
units.frag_end: human supervisor if the delay exceeds company policy—all without human intervention at each step.

units.why: "Users are responsible for verifying the accuracy of AI -generated information" tells users to check AI output for errors and bias, the P31 verification duty, binding all users, must.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for verifying the accuracy of AI -generated information

units.why: "users must comply with copyright and intellectual property laws, avoid infringement" is a rule on IP in AI output, so P52, must.
units.anchor: users must comply with copyright and intellectual property laws, avoid infringement

units.why: "AI -generated content should be viewed as a starting point, not the finished product" says output must be reviewed and edited, a verify-output rule (P31); P32 (student primary thinker) fits less since the sentence addresses review, not who thinks.
units.anchor: AI -generated content should be viewed as a starting point, not the finished product

units.why: "Confidential, sensitive, regulated data or non-public AU information must never be put into an open AI system" is a data-protection ban, so P50, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: must never be put into an open AI system

units.why: "AU login credentials must not be provided to, or shared with, AI Agents without written authorization from the CIO" protects credentials and concerns autonomous agents; I choose P50 (data protection) because the rule is about credential security, not general agent permission.
units.anchor: AU login credentials must not be provided to, or shared with, AI Agents

units.why: "The use of an AI system must be disclosed to capture institutional knowledge" requires disclosure of any AI use, so P24, must, require.
units.anchor: The use of an AI system must be disclosed to capture institutional knowledge
units.frag_start: The use of an AI system

units.why: "there must be documentation as to which code section is AI -derived and who reviewed it" marks AI-derived code at the place it is used, so P27, must.
units.anchor: there must be documentation as to which code section is AI -derived
units.frag_start: For example, if AI is used to create code
units.policy: If AI is used to create code and included in a larger section of code, there must be documentation as to which code section is AI-derived and who reviewed it.

units.why: "Disclosure should be considered when using AI in much the same way as citing a source in writing" compares AI to a cited outside source, P45, should.
units.anchor: in much the same way as citing a source in writing

units.why: "The use of an AI system must comply with any terms of use or contractual limitations" is a terms-of-use compliance rule with legal review, P52, must.
units.anchor: must comply with any terms of use or contractual limitations
units.frag_start: The use of an AI system must
units.frag_end: contractual obligations in using an AI system.
units.policy: The use of an AI system must comply with any terms of use or contractual limitations, and users should have terms or contracts for AI systems reviewed by the Legal Department.

units.why: "accessing AU data with or without authorization does not imply permission to use that data in AI models" limits feeding university data to AI, a data rule, P50, must-not.
units.anchor: does not imply permission to use that data in AI models
units.policy: Accessing AU data with or without authorization does not imply permission to use that data in AI models.

units.why: "The collection and use of human-related data should be based on informed consent" is a privacy and ethics rule for AI data use, P50, should.
units.anchor: should be based on informed consent
units.frag_start: The collection and use of human-related

units.why: "The user is responsible for determining whether privacy impact assessments need to be conducted" sets a privacy duty for AI projects, P50, must.
units.anchor: responsible for determining whether privacy impact assessments need to be conducted
units.frag_start: The user is responsible for determining
units.policy: The user is responsible for determining whether privacy impact assessments need to be conducted by AU through its relevant offices.

units.why: "AI should not replace human- centered approaches or be used for automated decisions in university processes" bars automated AI decisions in university processes; P46 covers only grades, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: AI should not replace human- centered approaches
units.policy: AI should not replace human-centered approaches or be used for automated decisions in university processes.
units.uncovered_note: AI must not be used for automated decisions in university processes (general human oversight, not limited to grading).

units.why: "Users who create content using artificial intelligence must clearly disclose the involvement of AI" requires disclosure for AI-created content, P24, must.
units.anchor: must clearly disclose the involvement of AI in the content creation process

units.why: "Faculty who develop instructional resources using AI ... shall acknowledge attribution" requires instructors to disclose AI-made course materials, P48, must.
units.anchor: Faculty who develop instructional resources using AI
units.policy: Faculty who develop instructional resources using AI and build assignments anchored in AI shall acknowledge attribution.

units.why: "Users may only transfer, disclose, upload, or share information in AI software" that policy permits, a restriction on what goes into AI tools, so P50 rather than P49, because it is not limited to course materials.
units.anchor: Users may only transfer, disclose, upload, or share information in AI software
units.policy: Users may only transfer, disclose, upload, or share information in AI software or AI enabled software or tools that is permitted under AU policies, federal and state laws and regulations, and AU policies and guidelines.

units.why: "instructors and faculty should explicitly outline their AI use expectations for students" tells instructors to state expectations in teaching materials, P09, should.
units.anchor: instructors and faculty should explicitly outline their AI use expectations for students
units.policy: Instructors and faculty should explicitly outline their AI use expectations for students, clearly defining the boundaries between acceptable and unacceptable uses.

units.why: "Students using AI must follow individual instructors' expectations" gives the per-instructor decision, so P04, must, and it binds students; it delegates rather than sets a rule.
units.anchor: Students using AI must follow individual instructors’ expectations

units.why: "All users will adhere to ethical principles through use of AI, such as fairness/mitigation of bias, accountability" lists ethical principles, P53, must.
units.anchor: All users will adhere to ethical principles through use of AI

units.anchor: must follow the AU Procurement of Information Technology Policy
units.policy: Users seeking to purchase or install software or tools that use AI technology must follow the AU Procurement of Information Technology Policy and its IT and Data Review Process.

units.why: "All AI tools in use at AU are subject to annual cybersecurity reviews" institutional review of AI tools, P65, informs.
units.anchor: All AI tools in use at AU are subject to annual cybersecurity reviews
units.frag_start: All AI tools in use at AU

units.why: "students will be provided with AI literacy guidance in the Student Handbook" commits offices to give students AI literacy resources; the closest type is P44 (teach AI use), chosen over P63 because the audience is students.
units.anchor: students will be provided with AI literacy guidance in the Student Handbook
units.policy: The Division of Enrollment & Student Affairs and the Division of Academic Affairs will ensure that students will be provided with AI literacy guidance in the Student Handbook and directed to augusta.edu/ai.

units.why: "Course syllabi will provide course-specific expectations for acceptable use" says each syllabus states AI expectations, P09, must.
units.anchor: Course syllabi will provide course-specific expectations for acceptable use

units.why: "Faculty, staff, and volunteers will be provided with AI literacy guidance" and annual training on AI supports employees in learning AI, P63, must.
units.anchor: compliance training for faculty and staff will include content specific to the use of AI
units.frag_end: generative tools for the department or function.
units.policy: Faculty, staff, and volunteers will be provided with AI literacy guidance during onboarding, and annual compliance training for faculty and staff will include content specific to the use of AI.

units.why: "Researchers are required to adhere to minimum disclosure standards for the use of AI in research and publications" sets research disclosure, P62, must.
units.anchor: Researchers are required to adhere to minimum disclosure standards
units.policy: Researchers are required to adhere to minimum disclosure standards for the use of AI in research and publications.

units.why: "All research using generative AI software or tools must be disclosed to IRB, AU AI governance committee" is a pre-approval disclosure rule for research, P62, must.
units.anchor: must be disclosed to IRB, AU AI governance committee
units.policy: All research using generative AI software or tools must be disclosed to IRB, the AU AI governance committee and the AU Division of Sponsored Programs before use.

units.why: "Any user aware of any conduct that may violate this policy has a responsibility to report it" is a duty to report violations. P36 is about classifying misconduct, not reporting, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: has a responsibility to report it
units.frag_start: Any user aware of any conduct
units.policy: Any user aware of any conduct that may violate this policy has a responsibility to report it.
units.uncovered_note: Duty to report suspected violations of the AI policy.

units.why: "Unintended upload or sharing of sensitive data with an AI system or tool must be reported to Privacy immediately" is a data-incident rule, P50, must.
units.anchor: must be reported to Privacy immediately

units.why: "The President will appoint an AI governance committee ... to ensure ethical use of AI" creates institutional governance, P56, admin.
units.anchor: The President will appoint an AI governance committee
units.policy: The President appoints an AI governance committee co-chaired by the Provost (or designee) and the CIO to ensure ethical use of AI and compliance and to review and determine any exception to this policy.

units.why: "The committee will also recommend revisions to this policy to align with updated regulatory requirements" is policy revision, P54, admin.
units.anchor: recommend revisions to this policy to align with updated regulatory requirements

units.why: "The Division of Information Technology will inventory AI tools" is institutional review of AI tools and vendors, P65, admin.
units.anchor: The Division of Information Technology will inventory AI tools
units.policy: The Division of Information Technology will inventory AI tools and conduct periodic audits of AI tools to assess adherence to ethical standards.

units.why: "The offices will develop and maintain guidance regarding the ethical use of AI for the academic environment" is institutional guidance, P56, admin.
units.anchor: develop and maintain guidance regarding the ethical use of AI for the academic environment
units.policy: The Office of Academic Affairs and the Office of Student Affairs will develop and maintain guidance regarding the ethical use of AI for the academic environment.

units.why: "All third -party AI vendors must provide documentation and assurance of ethical compliance" sets vendor review, P65, must.
units.anchor: must provide documentation and assurance of ethical compliance
units.policy: All third-party AI vendors must provide documentation and assurance of ethical compliance during procurement and renewal.

units.why: "guide the use of AI in producing scholarly communications ... should include disclosures of use and a thorough review" sets research and writing guidance, P62, should.
units.anchor: should include disclosures of use and a thorough review of the content generated
units.frag_start: The Office of Faculty Affairs will also

documents.title: Academic Honesty policy
documents.summary: General academic honesty policy whose definitions treat unpermitted AI text generators as cheating and AI-generated text presented as one's own as plagiarism. Instructors may grant explicit permission; the rest is a general integrity process.
documents.stance_why: The policy says "Students should not submit texts generated in part or full by artificial intelligence unless the instructor has granted explicit permission", so AI-generated text is barred unless permitted, which is restrict.

units.why: Cheating includes "using any technological device to gain or provide advantage ... without the permission of the instructor, including use of AI text generators", so unpermitted AI is misconduct, P36 (classification), must-not, restrict; P22 not chosen as it is not limited to exams.
units.anchor: including use of AI text generators
units.frag_start: Using any technological device to gain
units.policy: Cheating includes using any technological device to gain or provide advantage on an examination, lab practical, or other assignment without the permission of the instructor, including use of AI text generators.

units.why: "It also includes presenting content generated by artificial intelligence as one’s own" classifies this as plagiarism, P36, must-not, prohibit.
units.anchor: presenting content generated by artificial intelligence as one’s own
units.policy: Plagiarism includes presenting content generated by artificial intelligence as one’s own.

units.why: "Students should not submit texts generated in part or full by artificial intelligence unless the instructor has granted explicit permission" gives the fallback ban, P06 (default when no permission), should-not, restrict; P19 not chosen as the unit is about the permission condition.
units.anchor: unless the instructor has granted explicit permission
units.policy: Students should not submit texts generated in part or full by artificial intelligence unless the instructor has granted explicit permission to do so (e.g. in the syllabus or on the assignment prompt).

units.why: "Other acts of academic dishonesty may be defined by the instructor in their course syllabus" lets instructors add rules, P04, may.
units.anchor: may be defined by the instructor in their course syllabus

units.why: "The instructor must clarify in writing (for example, in the course syllabus) any situation peculiar to the course" requires written course expectations, P09, must.
units.anchor: The instructor must clarify in writing
units.frag_start: The instructor must clarify in writing

units.why: "If the student has any doubt about a course policy or the instructor's expectations, they should consult the instructor" tells students to ask first, P10, should (general to course policies including AI).
units.anchor: they should consult the instructor or the course director
units.frag_start: If the student has any doubt

units.why: "It is always assumed that all work produced or submitted in an academic context is the student's own" sets ownership of submitted work, P29, informs.
units.anchor: all work produced or submitted in an academic context is the student’s own
units.policy: It is always assumed that all work produced or submitted in an academic context is the student’s own and reflects original labor performed to satisfy the expectations assigned in that context.

units.why: "Meet with the student to discuss the concern and allow the student to respond" is the instructor step before action, P57, should; general integrity procedure that applies to AI cases.
